title: wonderful taste, easy "granola" recipe below
text:
The perfect coconut flakes, unsweetened, has a wonderful taste. Excellent price when you buy the case, store extra in your freezer.

Update.....8/2013.........this is a great product for diabetics, not to mention the healthy coconut oil that still remains in this product.

Easy Healthy Coconut Granola

2 cups coconut chips
1 cup nuts...cashews, sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds, pecans
¼ cup maple syrup
¼ cup honey
¼ cup coconut oil
1 tsp. vanilla
2 T. of chia seeds (great powerhouse little seed) or sub flax seed or leave these out.

Preheat the oven to 350 degrees.
Melt coconut oil, honey and maple syrup in a small saucepan until starting to bubble and simmer.
Add vanilla when you remove from the heat.
In a large bowl, mix the coconut chips and nuts and any optional ingredients if using.
Pour honey/maple syrup/coconut oil mixture over the dry ingredients and mix well. The consistency will vary some depending on the honey, coconut chips, and coconut oil you use. If there is not enough of the honey mixture to lightly coat all of the ingredients, add slightly more melted coconut oil and honey in equal parts.
Spread on a parchment paper lined baking dish.
Bake for 15-20 until starting to brown.
Remove and let cool, then crumble in to granola pieces.
Store in an air tight jar

title: Longtime Lavazza coffee drinker
text: I have been a Lavazza coffee drinker x >10 yrs. I was 1st introduced to Lavazza, mainly this Crema E Gusto, by a former employer. I'm not really into dark roast, so I prefer the Lavazza Qualita Rossa. Lavazza is the reason I became a 'just' black coffee drinker (I used to be addicted to Cafe Mocha from Starbucks)!! It's the only coffee brand I drink (w/ "occasional" Starbucks of course lol), as it is widely available (Quality Rossa & Crema E Gusto) in Canada. Here in the US, I believe only the other varieties (Classico, Perfetto) are available in selected grocery stores. I haven't tried those, but I'm sure they taste just as good. In between Lavazza, I drink Folgers, which IMO, has a very good taste as I can drink it w/o sugar and cream! Though Qualita Rossa is my fave, I ended up purchasing Crema E Gusto. I don't use a Moka pot (Er, coz I don't have one), but I use the Melitta 'pour over'. Lavazza makes a very good cup of coffee w/o adding sugar and cream! Highly recommend.

title: Best sardines available, more reasonably priced if you buy a case of one dozen here at Amazon
text: Through the years I have tried various brands of sardines. Wild Planet harvests and sells the best sardines and canned wild caught Pacific salmon I have ever tasted. These sardines are excellent in olive oil or in water, and my favorite are the ones in olive oil. I simply open a can slightly and pour out most of the oil to leave just a small amount to keep the sardines moist and fully tasty. However, they are in my opinion very overpriced on Amazon IF you want to buy just one can. The Wild Planet sardines in olive oil at a Walmart Superstore near me sell for $2.74 per can IF they are in stock at Walmart—exactly the same product shown here, $6.45 for ONE can, with free Prime delivery.  That is more than double the Walmart price. I believe amazon.com has done well to feature the Wild Planet products for a more competitive, lower price per can when purchased in the one-dozen case. It's one of those types of flavors that you want to put on everything, fingers included. We have eaten it on steak, the little bit that I had left from my daughter and have absolutely enjoyed this.

title: Decent quality tea, but may cause digestive issues for some
text:
Mugwort tea is purported to have several potential benefits ranging from helping with digestive system, to helping with energy. This mugwort tea comes in bags and recommends that one bag be steeped in one cup of 190 degree F water for one minute. Following the steeping instructions will result in a tea that is a light brown in color, smells a bit like bog water without the sulfur, and tastes like an earthy herbal tea which reminds me a bit of brussels sprouts. The tea doesn’t like to sink in water, so you will likely have to help it submerge so that it will actually steep (and there’s only a minute of steep time, so it's not like you can just wait around for it to eventually soak up the water on its own).

The tea bags come in a white bag that I think is plastic, but feels a bit like smooth paper. The bag is resealable and doesn’t allow a lot of light through, which should help keep the tea fresh. The particular bag I received was burned where the factory seal was placed, and while this didn’t have an impact on the tea itself, I think the factory could lower the temperature or reduce the time on the machine that seals these bags to prevent burning.

To me, the smell of the tea is not overly pleasant, but not necessarily off putting either. It smells herbal and earthy, like wetlands or a marsh. The taste has some of these similar qualities, but also has a hint of a vegetal quality to it, and reminds me a little of brussels sprouts. Generally, this isn’t an unpleasant tea, but certainly one that I will not think to reach for on a regular basis (although maybe it will grow on me). After drinking the tea, I didn’t really notice any extra energy or digestive changes, but after a second cup (steeped off the same bag), my digestive system seemed to be less happy.

If you haven’t tried mugwort tea, but are curious, this seems like a quality tea at a reasonable price. If you’ve never had mugwort before, I would recommend only having one cup and waiting to see how your body reacts to it. The tea has a relatively strong flavor, so going beyond the one minute steep time may be a bit much for some people. So while this may not be my preferred cup of tea, it wasn’t bad and I’ll wait and see if it ends up being something I learn to enjoy more over time.

text: I don’t do a full on keto diet, but because there is so much diabetes in my family I try to have 1 to 2 keto meals a day in an effort to keep my pancreas from getting worn out. I had tried the Magic spoon brand of keto cereals and found them extremely high priced and disgusting. My grandson who is nine years old, agreed with me. So I was really hoping this would be different. I’ll say it has a nice crunch. And the sweetness is OK at first, but then there is a definite aftertaste that just keeps going so by the time you’ve had three or four mouthfuls you don’t really want too much more. It’s not inedible, and I’ll likely eat it because I can . It will be around for a quick breakfast when I don’t have time for anything else. I do notice that because of the high protein content it does fill you up for quite a while and I’m not at all interested in eating until well after lunch. But I would not buy it again. My grandson won’t even consider it.  Not even for a bribe. As far as price goes, much more reasonable than magic spoon, and about the same on the flavor profile no better no worse.

title: Not cloyingly sweet, interesting choco-peanut puff snack
text:
A few days ago, I was offered a free 12-pack of Puffworks Dark Chocolate Organic Peanut Butter Puffs for review via the Amazon Vine Program, and I accepted.

I've had three bags of these over the past three nights since they arrived. I like them. They are definitely not the usual puff fare... there is this thin dark cocoa and peanut butter powder attached to very light, corn-based puffs. They are *just* sweet enough, but definitely not sugary sweet. You really get the flavor of the dark cocoa powder and peanut butter... the underlying puffs sort of blend in as the carrier, but they don't offer any flavor of their own. Unlike the photograph of the puffs in the description, the coating didn't make it to me very uniformly - there were many puffs missing large areas of the coating and there were also some clusters of puffs stuck together in the bags. Overall, they are tasty and I think you'll like them as long as you're not expecting something cloyingly sweet. At over $2 per 1.2oz bag, they are overpriced though.

I like milk thistle and it works well for cleansing the liver but the high estrogen content makes it unsuitable for everyday use. So I'm always on the lookout for a liver tea that uses different ingredients so I can switch it up but still do something on an everyday basis for my health.
I love this tea. I boil a teapot of water and just let one tea bag sit in it all day and I just drink the pot over the course of the day. It is slightly bitter but there's a fruity overtone to it, almost like grape. I really like the taste of it and more importantly, my liver is feeling much better

Unable to eat wheat, I brought this pasta with me on a visit to my sister's house, and her husband Paulie "the Goombah" refused to eat it.  At least, he thought he did.  He ate it, just didn't know it.  But here is one warning about this product:  if you are going to have it in a macaroni salad or similar, you should plan for hardly any leftovers.  It does not keep well in the fridge, becoming hardish and crunchy-ish and unappetizing.  I don't think it is the cold that makes it that way, because I store leftovers with marinara in the cold and it does not react the same way.  Maybe it is the salt in the salad dressing, or some other ingredient that reacts badly with the pasta.  But other than that this is a Godsend to folks who can't have regular pasta.

title: Cane sugar is NOT a GMO product.
text:
To much misinformation about GMO/Glyphosate in a comment. GMO is a genetically modified organism that has been genetically engineered to withstand being sprayed with glyphosate, AKA Roundup, and it will NOT be killed by the application. Non-GMO certifications means that the the product is NOT produced by a GMO plant. Most sugar used in the US, at this time, is from sugar beets that are Genetically Modified. USDA testing reveals GMOs in an increasing number of “certified organic products.” The newer Non-GMO seal initiated by the Non-GMO Project seeks to help consumers identify which organic products are really free of GMOs. In order to qualify for the seal, a product is rigorously tested by an independent third-party to ensure it meets the standard.
I saw one review on Kirkland Organic sugar that stated,” This is a great alternative to conventionally grown sugar. Conventionally grown sugar is sprayed with glyphosate in order to dry it out before harvesting.” This is an absolutely FALSE statement from someone that has no idea what GMO Certification, USDA certifications, or even what GMO really means. She continued,” So even if it is marked non-gmo you are still getting loads of glyphosate.” This is TOTALLY FALSE! If it is labeled Certified Non-GMO, then there is ZERO glyphosate used in the seeds or in the growing process.
GMO=genetically modified organism is a plant in which the seed has be modified to be able to withstand being sprayed by glyphosate, a herbicide that kills ANY plant it touches, but the certain plants such as corn, soy, cotton, Potatoes, Papaya, Squash, Canola, Alfalfa, Apples, and Sugar beets, to mane a few. So buying these that simply say “Certified USDA Organic” does NOT mean that they are free from the chemical glyphosate. Only a US Certification or different labels in other countries, guarantees that you are NOT eating RoundUP. The USDA certification is mostly attests that the food was not exposed to synthetic insecticide, fungicides, and synthetic fertilizers were not used.

title: Friends don't let friends melt their insides
text:
The Paqui One-chip Challenge is a self-imposed torture method for masochistic idiots, of which I was one. My boyfriend and I love spicy foods, so we Zoomed in my sister and my brother-in-law with milk, ice, and Tums at the ready. Popping this thing into your mouth tastes like crunching dry, spicy mud. The beginning hurts, but it's the aftermath that will haunt me. If you want to talk yourself out of it, here's how I ended up weeping on my bathroom floor:

- 7pm: 30 seconds after eating the entire chip, my boyfriend croaks "This was a horrible idea."
- 7:01pm: Eyes tear up angrily and mouths water. We're breathing in small bursts like we're giving birth.
- 7:02pm: The real sting hits, like actual heat burning your tongue. I'm making pitiful little sounds, squeaking "oh god it genuinely hurts." Involuntary, hacking coughs begin, as if our throats are trying to reject the spice to protect us.
- 7:03pm: My boyfriend and now I cry openly, smacking the counter, panting like dehydrated dogs.
- 7:04pm: Total body sweats take over, but we are too stubborn to quit before the 5 min mark.
- 7:05pm: My boyfriend paces around the apartment making caveman sounds - I can't speak any more.
- 7:06pm: We make it to 6 minutes when my boyfriend snatches his glass of milk and doesn't even care that he just let me win. I grab my milk right after him, but it does not ease the pain at all. Sucking on ice cubes helps, but it still hurts so bad. My 6'0" boyfriend folds himself in half and hobbles like a gremlin as quickly as he can toward our bathroom.
- 7:16pm: I check in to find my boyfriend breathing heavily, laying on his stomach on the bathroom floor. I tried to feed him some brown rice on the floor, while smugly thinking that men are such babies.
- 7:26pm: I abruptly stop our Zoom call when I begin bloating up like the Blueberry girl in Willy Wonka. It's my turn to make an embarrassing beeline for the bathroom. My boyfriend offers support and I scream "NO! please leave me!" and lock the door.
- 7:30pm: While my boyfriend is catatonic in the fetal position on the couch, I violently throw up everything in my stomach. It burns like lava coming back up through my throat and nose, and my body shakes with cold sweats. I slump down to lay on the cool bathroom floor and cry while my stomach rumbles like the spaghetti scene in Alien. I imagine that little silver monster breaking free.
- 8:00pm: I'm still horizontal and I realize my boyfriend hasn't made any noise in awhile. I weakly yell from the floor "Are you ok?!" He tiredly replies "Uh.. no. You?" I sadly mumble "Noooo. Definitely not." I drag myself to go lay down in a sad little ball next to him on the couch.
- 9-10pm: I refuse to go into the details of our following bathroom visits. Trust me, they were bad. Our bodies stayed in a physical state of emergency for a solid three hours.
- 11pm: We manage to eat a small amount of mild soup and go to bed. After four hours of the physical rebellion against our terrible choices, we were exhausted.

Don't do this to yourself. Don't let your friends do this to themselves. If you have a truly evil boss or an ex who wants to do this, maybe let them do it - but only if they're actually heinous people. These chips should be used as a torturous interrogation tactic, because if I were threatened with another one, I would tell anyone anything that they wanted to know. If you're going to do this anyway, eat a big greasy meal first, have ice cream ready for after, and get ready to learn the true meaning of regret.

title: Ladies and gentlemen, I present to you the newest weapon against your diet, new years resolutions, and tooth enamel
text:
This candy arrived in a golden sealed pouch which was thick and had a great ziplock to store your honeycomb goodies.

1st off the pieces are HUGE!!! like Gargantuan sized. I purchased them from Amazon because there is a chocolate shop here that introduced me to the confection. If you haven't yet tried chocolate dipped honeycomb sponge than please disregard the rest of the review, find the button that says "Buy now with 1-Click" and hold on to your seats because wow, its such a wonderful treat. honeycomb candy in general will have a light but very crunchy consistency and has the tendancy to melt down in your mouth as the sugar breaks down - like a crunchy cousin of cotton candy, but with a different texture and it doesn't warm up in your mouth as you eat it. ... Back to the review... These pieces came slightly covered with a dust of honeycomb with wasn't at all bad, but at first led me to believe that the candy was old or perhaps near going bad... its JUST FINE.

I found that I devoured a good bit more than I wanted to per sitting so I strongly advise only taking out ONE piece at a time otherwise you risk sugar overload - for the kids, I would instead recommend a half piece per sitting as this is a very rich tasting candy.

title: Nice roasted tea, better when made traditionally vs. just using a milk frother.
text:
I’ve had other Jade Leaf teas before and found them to be of good quality and a fair price. This hojicha powder keeps that reputation going for me. The flavor is good and the powder well ground, but you need to take care if you truly want it to be smooth (just like making a good matcha).

At first, I was being lazy and made this tea by eyeballing the right about off of a teaspoon into a cup, guessed at the right amount of cool water, and finished it off with a milk frother to mix it. The end result wasn’t bad, but it certainly could have been better. The flavor was good, but the texture was gritty (just like getting lazy with matcha). On subsequent mixings, I followed a much more traditional method of using a chawan (bowl), chashaku (spoon/scoop), and chasen (whisk) to mix the powder. This resulted in a much better mix and got rid of the grittiness, and it also improved the flavor a little. I then tried this method again and added a small amount of hot water to warm it up (as suggested on the package) and I found this to be pleasant (especially on cold mornings).

So I find this to be a good quality hojicha, and while I can’t claim to be an expert in hojicha, I certainly enjoyed this tea. I will say, with the smokey and more robust flavor, this tea may not be for everyone. It may be that coffee drinkers who are not into tea would like this. I liked the change of pace the roastiness of this tea brings to my day and seems to be a good pick-me-up.

title: Disappointing tea in a user-unfriendly box.
text:
I bought this as a little treat for myself and after all the glowing reviews, I could not wait to try the tea. Steeps three pots and a pretty gift-box to boot? Needless to say, I was excited to watch those tea blossoms form.

First annoyance: Dear lord, is that bamboo box a splinter hazard. The woven clasps at the side were incredibly difficult to get off and I had to be very careful handling the box itself all the while because the edges are sharp and they hurt!

Second annoyance: Superfluous and messy inner packaging. Bamboo is so renewable and environmentally-friendly that they decided, hey, what's more wasted paper inside the box?

Third annoyance: The teapot barely makes enough for one person.

Fourth annoyance: The tea blossom not only floats to the top as you pour hot water, it crumbles coming out of the plastic packet. And on the subject of the packets, I have no idea why "biodegradable tea bags" are listed as a product feature- there most certainly are none present.

Fifth annoyance: The most horrendous and unbelievably weak tea I have ever tasted. It was like boiled grass clippings and I can actually tolerate wheatgrass and spirulina. I've tried Stash, Choice, Guayakí, you name it, so I know how tea is supposed to taste.

Sixth annoyance: I did not even get to enjoy the visual splendour suggested by the dazzling pictures of tea leaves in full bloom. They do not open completely and the smell was unimpressive to say the least.

Given how awful the tea tasted, I'm beginning to question how "natural" the tea was in the first place.

If you want to go with organic, fair-trade, and interesting blends, try something along the lines of Zhena's Gypsy teas. At this price, I could have gotten the equivalent of 44 corn silk sachets.

I'd normally let something this lacklustre go and forget about it, but it infuriates me that this product is being marketed as some sort of luxury item when it is neither fun to drink nor to look at.

title: Movie Style Popcorn in the Comfort of Your Own Home
text:
We just LOVE this popcorn. We got introduced to it when I bought my wife a true popcorn machine (Great Norther 4oz Chaplain Popper and Cart). The popper and popcorn have been a wonderful addition to our home for the last 4 years and I have no plans to change any time soon.

The simplicity of the popcorn kit packaging is great. Premeasured popcorn, salt (with butter flavor), and oil (which is solid at normal ambient room temperature make this such an easy job of making popcorn any time we want it.

Turn on the kettle and let it heat up for 3-5 min. Squeeze out the oil and add the salt. I will say that if you use all the salt, it's quite a salty batch. We have found that using about half of the salt is about perfect. Wait till the oil is heated through and then add the popcorn. Pull down the kettle lid and wait.

Part of the fun for us is the magic of making our own popcorn. Our kids just can't not watch the machine do the work.

Now if one wants to complain that not all the kernels pop, I would argue that it's likely a combination of both the popcorn and the dimensions of your popping kettle. Do we lose some kernels? Yes (about 10%). Do I care? No. And why don't I care...

The TASTE and Quantity! Even with loss of some kernels, this 4 oz package will feed 2 adults and 2 kids (5 and 2) for an entire movie. Just the perfect amount for us too. As for the taste - I don't know how anyone can eat any other popcorn once they've tasted Great Northern. I simply refuse to eat the microwave popcorn that we might make because we just don't want to clean the popcorn machine after use. The secret to that amazing, delicious, and addictable popcorn taste? Coconut Oil. It seems like such a simple ingredient, but the popcorn flavor that it helps to generate is simply amazing.

The price is extremely reasonable too. And when I found that you could sign up for Amazon's subscribe and save, I signed up immediately. What a way to keep our machine fully stocked with the most authentic flavored movie popcorn ready for our weekly family movie night.

title: Fans of Sour Patch Kids Will Love This Deal
text:
If you're a fan of Sour Patch Kids, then there's no reason at all you won't absolutely love this remarkable packaging of two pounds of this original movie theater candy packaged in individual-sized, kid friendly packages of right around six pieces of candy in each smaller bag. This is completely awesome for taking a group of kids to a movie, handing out at Halloween, birthday parties, road trips, and so much more.

The candies themselves are an absolute delight - soft and chewy, gummy and sour candies that soften easily and taste awesome. Adults will love it for the nostalgia and kids will just plain love it.

There are five fun flavors/colors and each small package is right around .5 ounces of chewy and gummy delight.

The price point itself is a solid value when you consider the price of candy these days and certainly if looking at the price of movie theater candy. The candy's all fresh and nicely packaged and tastes amazing.

I wasn't sure if I would be satisfied here. I worried that the packaging would be plain or it would be some sour patch rip-off. It's not. It's nicely packaged and definitely takes me back to the days of going to the movies with my parents and those special candies that I always loved. I'm definitely loving these and I won't hesitate to get them again for those very special occasions. I definitely plan to have them around for family events and Halloween hand-outs. This is simply awesome!

title: Almost as good as eating a wonderfully ripe and delicious mango!!!
text:
Man, I only drank this once in my whole entire life many many many years ago at my friend's house when they still sold this stuff on the shelves at stores here in Hawaii and then never again.

Sadly shortly after that one time, I never saw this product being sold in stores here again. Yes, they have other powdered mango flavored drinks but it did NOT taste like this one did! This one tasted almost of pure sweet mango nectar, only thinner. What a perfect drink to have when mixed with some ice cold water on a hot and humid day like today!!!

It's so sad that this company decided this product is best for only foreign markets. Maybe they should've advertised and given out samples to gain interest. If they did and you love mangoes as much as I do, then you'd be instantly hooked! The nice thing is that this product already includes sugar so no extra sugar is needed! Amazing how sweet this product is without having a ton of sugar.

These packets make a 2 liter bottle's worth each so you get a lot of bang for your buck. Don't make the mistake like I did and pour out nearly half the pack into about 2 - 2-1/2 cups of water because this sucker is pretty sweet like a real ripe mango. Luckily just add more water to fix the problem and to suit your tastes!

title: I loved them!
text:
I am always looking for healthy, low calorie snacks, so when I heard about Popchips, I was intrigued. They are crunchy chips that are not fried, and not baked, but created using heat and pressure to make them pop into being. Since I love sweet potato chips in general, I thought I would give these a try.

The first thing I noticed was the color. They looked a bit lighter in color to other sweet potato chips I have tried, and I think this is due to them not being fried. They really looked the same color as fresh, cooked sweet potatoes. I did not notice any particular smell, other than good old sweet potatoes. So far so good.

In terms of taste, I thought they tasted great. The chips were nice and crispy, with only a hint of salt, so you really got to enjoy the naturally sweet flavor. I can really see that these will help satisfy cravings for something crunchy, something salty, something sweet, and especially something that is all three.

The texture is definitely not that of a typical potato chip. They are lighter, crisper, and airy, not as dense as a rice cake, but not as greasy as a typical chip. All in all, I was really pleased with them. Someone looking for a healthy replacement, or enjoys other veggie chip type snacks would really like these, I think. For a die hard chip lover, these would might not satisfy you upon first taste, but give them a couple of chances; personally I loved them.

With the snack size bag being 100 calories, I am pretty sold on these as a healthy snack alternative. This would be a great addition to a sandwich for lunch, or an in-between meal snack. I am happy to add Popchips to my snack rotation.

title: Really clumpy, product is more like clotted cream over half-n-half
text:
I use heavy cream for my morning coffee. When I get this cream, I can't pour any out because there is a huge fat cap at the top. So I use a chopstick to break up the fat cap and gently shake the container to redistribute, but then there are always inevitable chunks of clotted cream melting in the top of my coffee cup. The package advertises no added "gums", so I guess the gums have a purpose in the other brands.

Totally worth the extra dollar for Organic Valley brand cream to get a more consistent product, so we're switching back. It uses gellan gum to stabilize the cream, but gellan gum is a soluble fiber that some people take as a dietary supplement. So I have zero problems getting some trace amounts of extra dietary fiber in my coffee.

title: Great product. Mix with seltzer or water if too sweet.
text:
High protein is the only diet that works for me. I have tried almost every type of protein shake and, for me, the best milky-tasting ones are Premier Nutrition, available here on Amazon and also in Costco, and the Pure Protein cans available here on Amazon and also at Trader Joe's. Optimum Nutrition also makes a pretty good casein-based shake.

But all of these are milky tasting and slow to digest and, frankly, subject to extreme flavor fatigue.

I saw these Proasis protein shots at Rite Aid, bought one, chugged it down in the parking lot to see if it was any good, and then went back in and bought all 12--their entire stock.

Look, it's not like it tastes like the best fruit-flavored drink you've every tasted in your life, but it sure doesn't taste like any other protein shake or bar that I've ever tried.

Plus, I don't know what they did to make this happen, but this protein seems to be immediately available, and I get energy from it almost immediately. And, truly, I'm not as hungry. I have noticed cravings for carbs going down all by themselves! Pretty cool. And so far, these have caused zero stomach upset or bloating or dry-mouth, or any of the things that happen to me after those other shakes. Maybe it's because this protein is basically hypoallergenic.

What I love about these shots, is mixing them with a full can of plain seltzer, to make a protein-rich fruity spritzer. And then I can have a little ordinary-looking snack with my protein-rich spritzer to sip along the way and this is just a huge improvement over a thick chocolatey shake.

What I hate about them is they're expensive. And seriously overpackaged! But maybe that will change. After all, they're new.

title: A New Mexican girl living in Texas
text: Living in North Texas, it is hard to find the ingredients I am used to when preparing New Mexican food.  I found this product a few years ago and it is a must-have for my pantry.  But I will say that I have found I that adding a few extra ingredients to it enhances the flavor.  Some of the reviewers here say they were disappointed, but I suggest giving it another try by adding the following ingredients:  a small diced onion, extra salt from what the directions call for, 3 cloves of diced garlic, an additional dried red chile pod or two (I have these shipped to me from Nuevo Mexico and always have a bounty of them that I keep frozen for my red enchilada sauce)  and an extra half-pound of pork (I use lean boneless pork chops, diced into pretty small cubes).  It is because of the additions I felt needed to be made that I only gave this product 4 stars instead of 5.  I made this today and it was the perfect meal for the frigid day we had, with a brutal winter storm that moved through overnight!  Add some warm flour tortillas to top it off.

title: Does it rate?
text:
This is a ketchup I've been really looking forward to trying. Having read the reviews, here and elsewhere, there is pretty good agreement about its merits. Depending on where you look, some people concentrate on its similarity to Heinz, while others talk about how different it is. Here on Amazon, a lot of reviewers feel it's similar to Heinz, some even say it's the same. I expected it to be comparable. It isn't, except that both are good.

The difference is in the taste and consistency. The taste of Heinz is much more aggressive than Organicville. You could say it has more zing or kick. I'd imagine its vinegar and sugar content is pretty high. The consistency of Heinz is thicker, and yet smoother, sort of like paint. The Organicville feels lighter, and looks "grainier", though it is smooth, of course. It looks more "natural", while Heinz has a processed, technicolor look.

Neither is better than the other. They're two different animals. Having said that, I'm not sure I like the Organicville, at least on the hamburger I tested it on. I also tried it plain. So while I seemed to be enjoying the new and different taste and texture, and letting myself adjust to the more laid back material, by the last bit of my burger I wasn't dipping it in--and enjoyed that better.

Rating the item is actually easier than I thought. One star means "I hate it", two stars means "I don't like it". I certainly don't hate it, and I wouldn't say I actively dislike it. Five stars means "I love it", four stars means "I like it". I don't love it and I really can't say I like it, leaving 3 stars or "It's OK". I think it's better than ok. But somehow, it doesn't grab me.

title: Helping me indulge in an old favorite while dieting
text:
Deep fried ramen noodles soaked in high sodium sauces and broths aren't very conducive to weight loss, but instant noodles are one of my favorite things to eat, breakfast, lunch, or dinner. They're versatile and quick and highly customizable. I often have thought that if only I could buy just the seasoning packet, I could use my own non-fried noodles or even konjac noodles to really cut down on the carbs, calories, and fat without sacrificing the volume and experience of eating instant noodles. Between this product and the bulk Jin ramyun soup base powder that is also sold on here, I've been able to do just that.

You can even mix them together and make something like chapaguri/ramdon (though I think it's closer to the real thing if you add the bean powder to a pack of the stir-fried shin light as it's closer in flavor. The Jin powder has a slightly tomato-y flavor that I thought made it taste a little weird, but that is not this product's fault at all).

The real dish this powder is imitating is called jjajangmyeon, and it's normally made with a VERY oily sauce. I like that this is less so without sacrificing flavor. It's a bit different, but I like the earthy finish better actually. It's also a HUGE bag that I don't see myself running out of anytime soon. I opened it up and sealed it in an airtight container since the bag isn't resealable. Not a big deal for me. I'm just thrilled to have this as an option in my pantry. Don't get me wrong; it's not health food. I know the sodium is astronomical, so it's still mostly just a treat, but at least now I don't have to blow my whole calorie or carb budget on it when the craving strikes.

title: Love the apple
text:
I would HIGHLY recommend to try a single can to try from the grocery store/gas station before buying a whole case. So far of the 6 flavors I have tried, the only flavors that taste good are the Sour Apple and Orange Dreamsicle. I don't know what it is, but the rest have this weird "extra" taste to them.

Just be aware that these flavors are very strong. If you're looking for a light flavor, look elsewhere. Some people might not like that each one contains 300mg of caffeine (about 3 bottles of Mountain Dew.) But, these things keep me awake! As far as flavors in order of preference:

Sour green apple - My favorite! Just like drinking a green apple jolly rancher. Even my husband likes this flavor.
Orange Dreamsicle - Yum! This really does taste like an orange creamsicle.
Cotton Candy - It tastes like cotton candy. Not bad, but slightly "off" taste.
Peach Fizz - Meh. I love peach, but this is really strong peach, with a bit of a weird aftertaste.
Melon Mania - I just ordered a case of this and I wish I would have tried a single can from the store first. It’s a strange melon taste with a strong bad aftertaste. Disappointing.
Razzle Berry - Don't like this one at all. Like a blue raspberry with a weird "extra" taste that ends in a weird after taste.

title: Usually I love it but there have been times when batches have ...

title: Confidence in safe ingredients. Taste is great!
text:
Disclaimer: I am a relative of the One Culture Foods founder; that being said, I bought these from the One Culture Foods website just like any other public customer.

Before buying, I was already familiar with these sauce flavors. So what's different about these? I have a lot more confidence that the ingredients are wholesome and don't contain any unlabeled pesticides or other potentially dangerous chemicals that you never know about with conventional brands. That being said, the flavors still need to stand on their own. Happily, they most certainly do! My fiancee and I used the black bean sauce and gochujang sauce for braised meat, and we're using the sweet chili dipping sauce for salads, egg+avocado toast, and of course, dipping foods like raw veggies. I was worried that these sauces would be overly sweetened for the mainstream American market, but that's not the case--they're faithful to the originals, leaving room to add more sugar to your taste if you so choose. We loved these sauces and definitely plan to buy more when we run out!

title: Unique and tasty!
text:
Maybe I'm the right audience for this, maybe I'm not -- I do love coffee, but I drink it black and unsweetened most of the time. I will sometimes add a splash of cream, or some sugar, but I like coffee for being dark, roasty, and bitter. I didn't know what to expect with Bee 10, but I really enjoyed it!

It's simple to make, simply stir in with hot water and enjoy. I appreciate that it's really easy to dial in how strong you want it, and I had no issues dissolving the coffee in hot water at all. The taste? I was able to detect and taste the roasty notes of coffee that I like, and I really enjoyed the honey flavor as well. I didn't feel it was oversweet at all.

I'm going to keep it around for when I want something a little different, or we run out of coffee. I'd also love to try brewing and chilling it, it'd be a nice treat when it gets warmer out!

title: pizza and cinnamon rolls!
text:
This has worked SO unbelievably wonderfully! I honestly wasn't expecting much after having tried all of the 'pre-made' crap that stores try to feed the gluten-sensitive. THIS stuff makes food possible again! So far, I've made pizza, cinnamon rolls and flour tortillas out of it! The trick is to add 1 teaspoon of xanthan gum for every cup. More if you are wanting something stretchy like tortillas. I look forward to trying my hand at actual bread with this. I have tried the pre-measured BRM white bread, and it is great for toast, but I'm hoping this stuff works for sandwhiches.
My husband is hesistant to try anything gluten free after he tried the premade store stuff. But when he smelled the cinnamon rolls in the oven, he started drooling -and proceeded to eat 4 of them before the icing was even cooled! He didn't try the tortillas, but he has repeatedly asked me to make pizza for him again! :)
links to the recipes I used (it may take a little altering on your part. Adding 2 tablespoons of brown sugar and a pinch of salt to all recipes gives the flour a more 'flour' taste.)

title: This is Elegant!
text: Some months ago I found Khazana Rice on a lonely shelf at my local market. There was only one small bag left and because we were still in the middle of the very popular Dr. Fauci shutdown, it was the only actual bag of rice on the shelf, The rest were a few boxes of expensive flavored rice, or Minute Rice. I had never heard of it before so I picked up the Khazana. From my first experience I said to myself, this is "Rice from the Gods"! Well of course I had no idea who the God of Rice might be or had been, but if there is/was one, this is his or hers (sorry, that's as far as I go with pronouns). Lo and Behold I found that there is indeed a God of Rice. AND, I needn't have been so concerned about a pronoun because INARI is both Female and Male! Don't even ask about the other 50 or 70 genders, I just assume Inari is all of them. Must certainly be a heavy weight to bare for a God, with a sack of rice riding on the back of a fox just to make sure the rice we get is the best. Well Inari has done an exceptional job, and Khazana Rice has to be Inari's favorite! I had read about rice on store packages as being "long grain" before, but this was the first time I saw the term "Extra Long Grain". Long grain rice I had been used to was like, I don't know maybe 3/16"+ long. I liked the Long Grain because it seemed like more of a meal while the regular (what is regular?) seemed almost like Grits sometimes. Khazana Extra Long grain Rice is 'Elegant" when served on the table! The grains are a brilliant white (like a 6:00 PM TV News anchor's teeth!), and they are at least twice as long as other rice. The few times that I have served it to my guests, they have used that very term, Elegant! I bought this 10lb package because for some reason, it has disappeared from at least 3 of my local markets! Dr. Fauci? Putin? And I'm certainly not privy to any supply chain issues that are currently being felt. I sure hope President Biden sees this review. I do think he must like rice as it's a lot like ice cream only way warmer. Perhaps the President can sign an executive order, and soon this rice will be back on our market shelves! Let's hope America.....

title: Aversion Therapy
text: If you are feeling bad about restricting sweets these will make you feel worse. The box contains twenty four individually wrapped cookies. There are five flavors: lime-lemon, orange, apple cinnamon, passion fruit and chocolate.  The size is good but they are hard and dry. The lime one is the best with a pleasant flavor. The orange is passable, very subtle. I could detect no cinnamon in the apple just an assertive somewhat fake apple taste. The passion fruit was odd with a touch of tartness but the chocolate was the worst. It has no chocolate flavor just a weird, waxy, vaguely coconut oil taste. I did not like that these cookies contain both sorbitol and isomalt, a sugar alcohol that causes me digestive upset. If cookies are your dietary downfall these are effective aversion therapy. Unless you are a glutton for punishment look elsewhere for a sugar free treat.
